summary: Branch has 2 unmerged commits (2026-05-12) that rename model_performance.success_rate_percent → success_rate in DB setup scripts and add a schema-safe backfill migration. Three related PRs (274, 289, 703) covering the same fix were all CLOSED without merging. Main still uses success_rate_percent. It is unclear whether the rename was abandoned intentionally, applied via a different path, or simply never shipped.

commits.subject: fix: align model_performance success_rate field naming
commits.author: madzunkov@hotmail.com

commits.subject: fix: make model_performance success_rate backfill schema-safe
commits.author: madzunkov@hotmail.com

evidence.keyChange: Renames DB column success_rate_percent → success_rate in model_performance table; adds ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS migration + COALESCE backfill to avoid errors when legacy column is absent

risk.reason: Changes touch DB schema setup scripts. If the rename is still needed and was never applied, running setup scripts on a fresh DB could fail with column-mismatch errors. If the rename was intentionally abandoned (e.g. genome was updated to use success_rate_percent consistently), merging this would introduce a conflicting migration. Three prior PRs being closed without explanation is a yellow flag — could mean the underlying issue was resolved differently.

recommendation: Human review needed. Verify two things: (1) Does the live model_performance table have success_rate or success_rate_percent as the column name? (2) Does genome code (~/projects/genome/) reference success_rate or success_rate_percent when reading model performance? If genome references success_rate and the DB has success_rate_percent, this branch should be revived and merged. If they are already consistent, the branch is superseded and safe to delete.
